title: EEG Resting-state Microstates Correlates of Executive Functions
description: Resting-state EEG recordings from healthy young adults (165 recruited, 140 in the final sample) collected to test whether intrinsic brain spatio-temporal dynamics, measured as EEG microstates, relate to executive functions. Session 1 contains 5 minutes of alternating eyes-closed and eyes-open rest recorded with a 64-channel BioSemi system. Session 2 contains behavioral data from nine executive function tasks. The dataset supports correlating microstate metrics with mean z-scored executive function performance.
methods_description: Participants were seated in a windowless room facing a 24-inch screen and completed two sessions. Session 1 was a 5-minute resting-state EEG recording alternating between eyes closed and eyes open (30 s each), acquired with a 64-electrode BioSemi ActiveTwo amplifier at 512 Hz. Session 2 was a behavioral battery of nine tasks in fixed order: antisaccade, letter-memory, color-shape, number-letter, Stroop, keep-track, dual n-back, category switch and stop-signal. Data were collected at the Centre de Neuroergonomie, ISAE-SUPAERO, Toulouse, from February 2022 to July 2023.
